name: Norway

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally
paths.note: Dividends and share gains are multiplied by 1.72 and taxed at 22% (37.84%), with credit for foreign withholding tax; net wealth tax of 1.0% (1.1% above NOK 43 million for a couple) on 80% of the value of shares. No inheritance or gift tax; the children take over the cost basis.

paths.name: Holding company (AS)
paths.note: A Norwegian AS owned by the parents pays no tax on gains on qualifying (Norwegian and EEA) shares and funds and 0.66% on their dividends (fritaksmetoden); personal tax of 37.84% falls on payouts. The parents still pay wealth tax on the AS shares. The tax file assumes the foreign portfolio sits in EEA-domiciled funds or shares; direct US shares would be taxed at 22% in the AS. The AS shares are in the estate; there is no inheritance tax.

checks.working: Top marginal case; the shielding deduction (cost basis x risk-free rate) is ignored, i.e. the cost basis of the shares is taken as negligible. Dividends 200,000 x 1.72 = 344,000 taxed at 22% = 75,680 (Skatteloven § 10-11; Skatteetaten: factor 1.72, effective 37.84% for 2026), less the 15% foreign withholding credited (§ 16-20) = 30,000, = 45,680. Gains 150,000 x 1.72 x 22% = 56,760 (§ 10-31). Wealth tax 2026: shares count at 80% (20% valuation discount) = 8,000,000; allowance for spouses taxed jointly 2 x 1,900,000 = 3,800,000 (thresholds doubled; Skatteetaten, Formuesskatt); 4,200,000 x 1.0% (municipal 0.35% + state 0.65%) = 42,000. Total 45,680 + 56,760 + 42,000 = 144,440.

Assumes the AS holds Norwegian or EEA shares and EEA-domiciled funds, which qualify for the participation exemption (Skatteloven § 2-38; PwC, Norway Corporate income determination); US shares held directly would be taxed at 22%. Gains of 150,000 are exempt (0). Dividends: 97% exempt, 3% taxed at 22% = 0.66% x 200,000 = 1,320; no credit for foreign withholding is used (tax file). The AS pays no wealth tax; the parents do on the AS shares, valued at the company's net value (10,000,000) less the 20% share discount = 8,000,000; less the couple's allowance 3,800,000 = 4,200,000 x 1.0% = 42,000. Total 1,320 + 42,000 = 43,320. The AS's running costs are not in the tax file; payout tax of 37.84% excluded.

Norway abolished inheritance and gift tax on 1 January 2014 (PwC, Norway Other taxes). NOK 100,000,000 passing to three children: tax 0. The children take over the cost basis, so tax on latent gains falls on their later sales.
The AS shares pass like any asset and Norway has no inheritance or gift tax since 1 January 2014 (PwC, Norway Other taxes): tax 0 on NOK 100,000,000 for three children.

assumptions: Top marginal case: about EUR 600k of dividends a year. The cost basis of the shares is taken as small, so the shielding deduction is ignored.
The reference couple is taxed jointly for wealth tax: allowance NOK 3.8 million and 1.1% from NOK 43 million of net wealth (tax file corrected from the single person's NOK 1.9 million).
The AS holds the foreign portfolio through EEA-domiciled funds or shares, so gains are exempt and dividends bear 0.66% (tax file assumption; BFU 5/2026 shows a US fund held by an AS is taxable).
The portfolio enters the AS with no Norwegian tax on its latent gains.
The 2027 budget proposals (allowance NOK 1,990,000) are not law and are not modelled.
open_questions: Needs an engine change: the primary home counts at 25% of its value in the wealth-tax base (70% above NOK 14 million); the engine values shares at 80% but counts the home in full, overstating wealth tax a little.

Needs an engine change: the shielding deduction (skjermingsfradrag, skatteloven § 10-12) deducts cost basis x risk-free rate (3.6% for 2025) from dividends and gains before the 1.72 factor and carries the unused part forward; the family's cost basis is unknown and the engine has no cost basis, so a basis of NOK 30 million would shelter more than the whole annual dividend.

Needs an engine change: moving an existing portfolio into an AS is a realisation at 37.84% on the latent gain (Norway gives no step-up on arrival); the projection starts with the full portfolio inside the AS.

Structure considered and rejected: the share savings account (ASK) holds only EEA-domiciled shares and funds, defers tax until withdrawals above cost and taxes them at 37.84% (Skatteetaten); the engine cannot tax a payout in proportion to the gain, and most of this portfolio is not EEA-domiciled.
Skatteloven article numbers (§ 10-11, § 10-12, § 10-31, § 16-20) were given from memory and not opened on a statute page.
A foundation or trust is not a common Norwegian vehicle for a private portfolio and was not researched.
